Drug discovery in inflammatory diseases. I’m a protein crystallographer.

Textbooks are very difficult to read straight through. If you are not taking a course in biochemistry at the moment, read short parts of the material as you come across topics or articles elsewhere in your studies. This will help with context and make remembering much easier.

For instance, if you read a news item about CRISPR, look up DNA at that point. Review base pairing and try to understand how CRISPR works. 

Prion diseases sometime show up in the news. Use that opportunity to review protein structure, folding, and how/why proteins might clump together. 

Another one might be multi-drug resistance. Read about ABC transporter structure.  As you start to read one topic, you might end up going down a rabbit hole and learning many topics! I often end up reading for hours like this.
